examples.ko: 이 가방은 디자인이 좋지만 너무 값비싸요.
examples.en: This bag has a nice design, but it's too expensive.
The thought matters more than an expensive gift.
I bought expensive clothes and regretted it.
The food here is pricey, but the taste is guaranteed.

examples.ko: 저 가게는 물건이 다 값비싸서 구경만 했어요.
examples.en: Everything in that shop is expensive, so I just looked around.
He is wearing a watch that looks expensive.

explain: '비싸다'와 비슷하지만 '값비싼 보석'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 때 고급스럽고 귀한 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '값싸다'예요. '값비싼, 값비싸요, 값비싸서'로 활용해요.

phrases.en: I use expensive things carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 귀하고 비싼 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it gives a feeling of something precious and costly.

phrases.en: It was too expensive, so I couldn't buy it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비싼 것이 이유일 때 이어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the high price as a reason.

phrases.en: This restaurant isn't expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 가격이 부담스럽지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, saying the price is not a burden.

explain_en: It is like '비싸다', but when it modifies a noun, as in '값비싼 보석', it feels luxurious and precious. The opposite is '값싸다'. It conjugates as '값비싼, 값비싸요, 값비싸서'.

examples.en: My grandfather gave me a gold watch as a gift.
I want a gold watch as a graduation present.
My father used to wear this gold watch.
I went to the wedding wearing a gold watch on my wrist.
Even a gold watch gets a worn strap if you wear it for long.

examples.ko: 금시계 한 개 값이 얼마인지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you know how much a single gold watch costs?

explain: 시계는 손목에 '차다'라고 해서 '금시계를 차다'가 자연스러워요. 색만 금색인 시계는 '금색 시계'라고 하고, '금시계'는 금으로 만든 시계를 말해요. 비싼 물건이라서 선물이나 어른 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My father always wears a gold watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계는 손목에 '차다'라는 동사를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For watches on the wrist, the verb used is '차다'.

phrases.en: A gold watch is too expensive, so I can't buy one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금으로 만든 물건이라서 값 이야기가 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since it is made of gold, its price often comes up.

phrases.en: I gave my wife a gold watch for our wedding anniversary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 날에 주는 값비싼 선물로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often mentioned as a costly gift for a special day.
phrases.en_equiv: give a gold watch as a gift

explain_en: A watch is worn with the verb '차다', so '금시계를 차다' is the natural phrase. A watch that is only gold in color is a '금색 시계', while '금시계' is made of gold. It is expensive, so it often comes up in talk about gifts and elders.

examples.ko: 자전거 대여료는 한 시간에 삼천 원이에요.
examples.en: The bike rental fee is 3,000 won per hour.
The rental fee was pricier than I thought, so I just bought one.
Insurance is included in the daily rental fee.
Can I pay the rental fee by card too?
Besides the clothing rental fee, you also need a deposit.

examples.ko: 대여료를 조금 깎아 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lower the rental fee a little?

explain: 자전거, 옷, 장비, 자동차처럼 잠깐 빌릴 때 내는 돈이에요. 집이나 건물을 오래 빌리는 값은 보통 '임대료'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I paid the camera rental fee first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌릴 때 돈을 내는 상황에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for paying money when you borrow something.

phrases.en: The rental fee here is cheaper than other places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값을 비교하거나 평가할 때 써요. '비싸다'로 바꿔도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare or judge the price. You can swap in 'expensive' (비싸다).

phrases.en: How much is the rental fee for this umbrella?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 빌리기 전에 값을 물어볼 때 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A handy question to ask the price before renting at a shop.
phrases.en_equiv: How much is the rental fee?

explain_en: It is the money you pay to borrow things like bikes, clothes, equipment or cars for a short time. The price of renting a house or building long-term is usually called '임대료'.

examples.en: One bundle of pencils is two thousand won.
I tied the newspapers into bundles and put them out.

examples.ko: 이 묶음은 열 개가 한 세트예요.
examples.en: This bundle is a set of ten.

examples.ko: 꽃 두 묶음을 사서 꽃병에 꽂았어요.
examples.en: I bought two bunches of flowers and put them in a vase.

examples.ko: 편지 한 묶음이 책상 위에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A bundle of letters is lying on the desk.
Bundled products are discounted separately at the supermarket.

explain: '한 묶음, 두 묶음'처럼 세는 말로도 써요. 대파나 시금치 같은 채소는 '한 단'처럼 다른 세는 말을 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a bundle of pencils.
phrases.nuance_ko: '묶음'을 세는 말로 써서 물건의 수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a counter to say how many bundles of something there are.

phrases.en: These socks are sold as a bundle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개를 한꺼번에 묶어서 판다는 뜻으로, 가게에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means selling several items together as one bundle; common in shops.

phrases.en: Bundled products are cheaper than single items.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개를 한 묶음으로 만든 물건을 말할 때 뒤에 '상품'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '상품' after it to refer to items sold together as one bundle.

explain_en: It also works as a counter: 한 묶음, 두 묶음. For vegetables like 대파 or 시금치, a different counter, 한 단, is also used.

en: to give service; to provide service

examples.en: This shop gives a drink for free.
The owner gave us dessert on the house.
The company plans to offer service in Korean, too.
The new app will be offered starting next month.
Many shops give things to customers for free.
The game that had run for a long time ended this year.

explain: 한국에서 '서비스'는 가게에서 덤으로 주는 것이라는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. '서비스로 주세요'처럼 말해요. 그래서 '서비스하다'도 공짜로 주는 것이나 앱, 게임을 제공하는 것을 말해요.

phrases.en: The owner gave us a drink as a free extra.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서비스하다'보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily speech than '서비스하다'.

phrases.en: Please give us a drink as a free extra.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 덤을 부탁할 때 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to ask a shop for a freebie.

phrases.example: 이 앱은 여러 나라에서 서비스하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This app is offered in many countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 게임을 제공하는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for offering an app or game to users.

explain_en: In Korea, '서비스' is also commonly used for a free extra a shop gives you, as in '서비스로 주세요'. So 서비스하다 can mean giving something free or running an app or game for users.

examples.ko: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전기세가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In summer the electricity bill is high because of the air conditioner.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기세를 아직 못 냈어요.
examples.en: I have not paid this month's electricity bill yet.
The electricity bill is taken out of my account automatically every month.

examples.ko: 전기세 걱정 때문에 난방을 조금만 틀었어요.
examples.en: I worried about the electricity bill, so I used the heating only a little.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 전기세보다 가스비가 더 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In winter the gas bill is higher than the electricity bill.
Both electricity and water bills went up, so living costs are a burden.

explain: '세'는 원래 세금이라는 뜻이지만 일상에서는 '전기세', '수도세'처럼 요금도 이렇게 말해요. 고지서에는 '전기요금'이라고 적혀 있어요. '전기세를 내다', '전기세가 나오다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I pay the electricity bill at the end of every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요금을 돈으로 낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you pay the bill with money.

phrases.example: 겨울에는 난방 때문에 전기세가 많이 나와요.
phrases.en: In winter, the electricity bill is high because of heating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요금이 많이 나왔다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bill turns out to be high.

phrases.en: The electricity charge is written on the bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전기세'보다 조금 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal word than 전기세.

explain_en: '세' originally means tax, but in everyday speech people also call bills this way, as in '전기세' and '수도세'. On the bill itself it is written '전기요금'. It goes with '전기세를 내다' (pay) and '전기세가 나오다' (the bill comes).

examples.en: I'll pay for this meal by card.
I pay the rent at the end of every month.
I paid the price and got a receipt.
Please tell me how much I have to pay.

examples.ko: 이미 지불한 돈은 돌려받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Money already paid can't be refunded.

examples.ko: 현금으로 지불하면 오백 원 깎아 줘요.
examples.en: If you pay in cash, they take off five hundred won.

explain: '내다'보다 딱딱한 말이고, '계산하다'가 계산대에서 값을 치르는 상황인 데 비해 '지불하다'는 돈을 건네는 일 자체를 말해요. 서류나 안내문에 '지불'이 보여요. 비슷한 '지급하다'는 월급이나 보험금처럼 받을 사람에게 돈을 내줄 때 써요.

phrases.en: I paid the hotel fee in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값을 내야 하는 때보다 먼저 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when paying before the payment is due.

phrases.en: I usually pay in cash.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여 돈을 내는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-으로' to say the method of payment.

phrases.en: I chose a card as my payment method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑 앱이나 안내문에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in shopping apps and notices.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '내다'. Where '계산하다' is about settling the bill at the register, '지불하다' is about handing over the money itself, and '지불' shows up on forms and notices. The similar '지급하다' is for paying out money someone is owed, such as wages or insurance.

dis.h: formal pay for a purchase or service

p.n: 내다 is casual and the most natural in speech.

en: to give a discount; to reduce

examples.en: This shop discounts clothes every weekend.
They discounted these clothes by 30 percent last week.
They give students a 10 percent discount.
If you discount the price, customers increase.
Do you give a discount if I pay by card?
I bought it at the discounted price, so I feel good.

explain: 가게가 정가를 내리는 건 '할인하다'이고, 손님이 값을 깎아 달라고 할 때는 '깎아 주세요'라고 해요. 시장에서는 '좀 깎아 주세요'가 흔한 말이에요. 내린 가격은 '할인가'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The shop gives students a 10 percent discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게가 손님에게 값을 내려 준다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a shop lowers the price for a customer.

phrases.en: You can buy it at the discounted price now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내린 가격을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the reduced price.

phrases.en: They discounted these shoes last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 값을 내렸다는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for a price that has already been lowered.

explain_en: When a shop lowers the list price, that is 할인하다. When a customer asks for a lower price, they say '깎아 주세요' (please knock it down), which is common at markets. The reduced price is called '할인가'.
